🚨🇲🇽 <u>Segob: Organized Crime Paid Protesters to Block Santa Fe</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez confirmed federal authorities are investigating payments by a criminal group — allegedly ordered by an inmate of Federal Prison No. 4 in Nayarit — to people who blocked Santa Fe demanding "better conditions" for prisoners. Both those who paid and those who organized will be investigated. "It cannot be that they are paying people to block roads, especially people totally linked to organized crime."
banner: SANTA FE BLOCKADE: CRIME MONEY PROBED

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Old Bosses of the INE Now Demand "Consensus" — As the ASF Audits Their Years</u>

José Woldenberg, Luis Carlos Ugalde, Leonardo Valdés and Lorenzo Córdova — four former heads of IFE/INE — asked the Chamber of Deputies to name the new INE president "by consensus" and to rethink the makeup of the General Council. The call lands as the ASF prepares a review of INE procurement from 2000 to 2025, the exact span of their tenures, and after the INE itself filed an FGR complaint over electoral-materials contracts. Ugalde joined by video from Boston, where he has lived for a year and a half.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>400-Meter Huachicol Tunnel Found Under Mexico City, Blocks from the Airport</u>

Crews repairing a sinkhole in Venustiano Carranza's colonia 20 de Noviembre found a hose running two blocks underground. It led to a tunnel of more than 400 meters feeding a clandestine diesel tap inside a house on Calle Cerámica, a few blocks from Circuito Interior and the AICM. Pemex Strategic Safeguarding, the Guardia Nacional and CDMX police sealed the site, and the FGR opens a case for theft of fuel "considered the nation's patrimony."

🇲🇽📉 <u>CEPAL: Without the Universal Pension, Mexico Would Have 11.5% More Poor</u>

CEPAL's Social Panorama of Latin America 2026, released today, names the non-contributory pension for older adults — the heart of AMLO's project — as decisive in Mexico's poverty drop: without it, the number of poor would be 11.5% higher. People over 65 now have the lowest poverty rate of any age group. Mexico was also the second country in the region that most narrowed its income gap between 2019 and 2025, cutting inequality 1.2 points a year against a Latin American average of 0.7.

🇲🇽💵 <u>Minimum wage 2027: anti-poverty group asks for 345 pesos a day</u>

Acción Ciudadana Frente a la Pobreza asked Conasami for a 2027 minimum wage of 345 pesos a day, about 10,500 a month, up from 315.04 today (El Economista). The 2026 wage buys 1.95 basic baskets; 345 pesos would buy 2.09, on the way to the government's goal of 2.5 by 2030. The group also wants the SAT and IMSS to stop withholding from low wages: "every extra peso companies pay must reach workers' pockets in full." Conasami votes starting December 1.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>Sheinbaum goes viral in China: 21 hours, economy class, to APEC</u>

Mexico's president reached the APEC summit in Shenzhen the way she always travels: on a commercial flight, in economy. She went Mexico City to Tijuana, then China Southern CZ8032 to Shenzhen, about 21 hours in total. Chinese social media lit up. The presidential jet AMLO inherited was sold off years ago. At this summit she met Xi, Carney, To Lam and Trump.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Measles: Mexico down to 14 active cases after 40.9M vaccine doses</u>

Mexico now has 14 active measles cases, 12 in Chiapas and 2 in Quintana Roo, says Health Undersecretary Rafael Valdez. A national campaign applied about 40.9 million doses across 2025 and 2026. Twelve states have gone three months without a single case. "Of the 18 countries in the region with active transmission, Mexico is the second-lowest." Another 10.8 million free doses are ready at more than 21,000 vaccination points.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>781-person caravan held in Chiapas: INM care, no repression</u>

A caravan of 781 people, mostly Hondurans and Salvadorans, remains in Mapastepec, Chiapas, under INM care. Some have already chosen to go home. Others are being offered regularization, including minors with Mexican parents, or referral to COMAR for asylum. Segob says the policy rests on "unrestricted respect for human rights" and family unity. Of the 24 caravans that have entered since Trump's second term began, zero reached the US border.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico and the US float a regional migration summit</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez met US Ambassador Ronald Johnson, and both sides put a regional summit of migration authorities on the table to coordinate on flows from Central America. Rodríguez said the response was favorable on both sides; no date or participant list yet. The proposal follows Trump's threat to double tariffs over caravans. Rodríguez added that Mexico keeps open security channels with Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum and Trump meet in Shenzhen, agree to talk again at the G-20 in December</u>

On the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen, Sheinbaum and Trump held a roughly 20-minute meeting focused on trade. Sheinbaum called it "very good" and said the T-MEC negotiations are "very advanced." They agreed to meet again at the G-20 summit in the US in December. She also put a number on the table: US border encounters with migrants are down 96%. That comes days after Trump threatened to double tariffs over caravans that never reached the border.
